general.temas: The US air traffic disruption and its effects are the most frequently covered topic. Other recurring stories concern the court case over the 6x1 working week, Brazil’s defeat to Japan, the pope’s visit to Peru and diabetes. Only CartaCapital highlights the increase in violence in São Paulo schools.
general.motivo_crispacion: The tension stems from protests in France and Portugal over the economic crisis, a police law and housing prices. In Brazil, the opposition sees risks in Lula’s plan to create a National Guard, while the Supreme Court examines changes to the working week. Internationally, Zelensky mentions a US proposal that would involve the cession of Ukrainian territory. Stories about health, culture, sport and recipes partially offset these contentious issues.

Folha de S.Paulo.resumen:
- The Miss Universe final will return to Brazilian free-to-air television in 2026.
- A municipal bill envisages new benefits for São Paulo’s municipal attorneys; the Supreme Federal Court will bring the case on the 6x1 working week before its full bench in person.
- A US air traffic control failure affected flights from Brazil; another story examines the Brazilian system.
- The front page covers diabetes treatments, changes in Cosan’s leadership and a decline in Black Friday advertising.
- It includes a historical note on Washington Luís, a favorable assessment of Fernando Henrique Cardoso and film and food news.
Folha de S.Paulo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although “perks” carries a disparaging connotation and expressions such as “revolutionized” and “red flag” add emphasis; there is no apparent contrast drawn between the people and the elites.
Folha de S.Paulo.sesgo: The wording about the municipal bill presents the benefits in critical terms, while the text about Fernando Henrique Cardoso offers a laudatory assessment. The selection combines politics, the economy, health and entertainment, without showing a clear overall bias.

O Globo.resumen:
- The Supreme Federal Court’s full bench will review the decision on ending the 6x1 work schedule; Dino advocates collective bargaining for the transition.
- Rio hosted the Longevity Games, restricted parking in Copacabana and resumed mpox vaccination for certain groups.
- Romário called for Ancelotti’s departure after Brazil’s defeat; Zidane became irritated by questions about Mbappé and a boxer reassured his followers after an injury.
- “Guerreiras do K-pop” announces a world tour; “Sob o mesmo sol” triumphs at Cine Ceará and rock bands perform for passengers affected by flight cancellations.
- Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the election for governor of Alaska.
O Globo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although expressions such as “air travel chaos” and “disfigured” add drama and sensationalism.
O Globo.sesgo: The selection gives prominence to local service news in Rio, sports and entertainment, alongside the labor transition. There is no clear partisan political bias in the headlines.

O Estado de S. Paulo.resumen:
- Air traffic between Brazil and the United States is beginning to return to normal after a shutdown.
- Management failures and the Huang case weaken Trump ahead of a meeting with Xi and Putin.
- The front page covers the government’s economic challenges and rare earths.
- There are protests in Portugal over housing and in France over the economic crisis and a police law.
- Sports and entertainment coverage includes the Brasileirão, a tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo, GTA 6 and figures from film and music.
O Estado de S. Paulo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although expressions such as “a show of his own,” “silver bullet” and “so big” add emphasis or appeal; there is no apparent confrontation between the people and the elites.
O Estado de S. Paulo.sesgo: The selection combines international affairs, the economy and protests with sports and entertainment. The political and economic headlines take a critical or interpretive approach, but no clear ideological orientation emerges from the selection as a whole.

Gazeta do Povo.resumen:
- The Vatican calls for peace in Europe to be prioritized; the pope celebrates Mass in the Andes and a diocese creates a fund for immigrants.
- Turnout is rising among voters for whom voting is optional; the Workers’ Party proposes new taxes and Lula reaffirms his plan for a National Guard.
- Fachin supports appointing a Black woman to the Supreme Federal Court; a road link in Santa Catarina is moving forward and Claro takes over the Senate’s telephone services.
- A meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi is announced; the US attributes an air traffic shutdown to a cable replacement.
- Writer Michel Houellebecq is under investigation for alleged Islamophobia.
Gazeta do Povo.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although the headline about Houellebecq contrasts his novel with the investigation, and the one about the National Guard highlights the risks identified by the opposition.
Gazeta do Povo.sesgo: The selection gives prominent attention to the Catholic Church and presents government and Workers’ Party measures alongside their possible effects or criticisms. No conclusive political bias is apparent from these headlines alone.

CartaCapital.resumen:
- The pope defends the social role of science in Peru; Microsoft restores Outlook and Teams after a global outage.
- Zelensky says the US is proposing the cession of Ukrainian territory in exchange for NATO membership.
- Lula talks about democracy and critical minerals in the Philippines; Moraes requests details about Bolsonaro’s security and a person convicted over January 8 dies.
- Recorded incidents of violence in São Paulo state schools rose by 73.83% in 2025.
- Brazil’s defeat to Japan prompts criticism from Romário and comments from Ancelotti; Camila Ferezin is named coach of the year.
CartaCapital.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although expressions such as “ruins everyone’s life” and “blasts,” together with the quoted insult from Romário, add drama and sensationalism.
CartaCapital.sesgo: The front page combines political and international news with sports and service topics. The contrast in opinions about the Brazilian national team stands out, without any unequivocal political orientation being apparent.

opiniones.comunista:
The interruption of the court case on ending the 6x1 working week reminds us that time, too, is an arena of class struggle. For those who live on their wages, rest is not a privilege: it is a condition for health and family life. I support a shorter working week and collective bargaining with strong unions, not a transition dictated by the demands of capital.

I also welcome proposals to tax great fortunes and dividends, but raising revenue is not enough: those resources must strengthen public services and expand collective ownership, so that socially produced wealth meets social needs. Mpox vaccination in Rio and advances in diabetes treatment show why healthcare cannot depend on the ability to pay.
opiniones.anarquista:
Today I see a struggle over the time working people have to live their lives: the Supreme Court suspended the vote on the transition to ending the 6x1 schedule. Reducing working hours is necessary, but I do not want the freedom to rest to depend solely on judges, governments or parties. Collective bargaining is worthwhile if it comes from organized workers, with autonomy from employers and leaders, and a real ability to make decisions.

Meanwhile, São Paulo’s municipal government is proposing benefits for its municipal attorneys and the president is reaffirming his plan for a permanent National Guard. I distrust a power that distributes privileges within its institutions and seeks to strengthen its instruments of coercion. I prefer to build security and well-being from the bottom up: through mutual aid, services managed by their communities and workplaces where no one has authority over anyone else.
opiniones.liberal:
I am concerned by how easily politicians find new uses for other people’s money. The bill creating benefits for São Paulo’s municipal attorneys deserves rigorous scrutiny: before expanding benefits, their necessity and cost to taxpayers must be justified. Likewise, proposals to raise taxes on income and wealth can discourage the saving and investment that sustain growth. I prefer a limited state, responsible public finances and low taxes.

I also believe that a shorter working week is a legitimate aspiration, but simply decreeing it is not enough. The transition away from the 6x1 system should allow for agreements that address the different circumstances of workers and businesses. More rest is desirable; so too are preserving jobs and giving people greater freedom to decide how they work.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I see the proposal for a permanent National Guard as an opportunity to strengthen security, but I would not give the government a blank check: I want transparent command, legal oversight and respect for the states’ powers. Public security forces must protect Brazilians, not become an instrument of any political project.

I am also concerned that, while new taxes on income and wealth are being proposed, São Paulo is considering additional benefits for municipal attorneys. Before asking more of taxpayers, the elites should justify every privilege. And on ending the 6x1 working week, I support rest and family life, but I reject any disregard for the impact on those who produce and create jobs. Brazil needs decisions debated openly, not solutions imposed from judges’ chambers or sold as inevitable by politicians and the media.
opiniones.centro:
The discussion about ending the 6x1 working week deserves fewer slogans and more agreements. I believe working fewer days can improve the lives of millions, but a responsible transition must listen to workers and businesses alike. Collective bargaining offers a way to adapt the changes without giving up labor protections. The Supreme Court’s examination of the issue at an in-person full-bench session is part of how institutions function, not a reason to turn every disagreement into a crisis.

I am also concerned about the proposal for new benefits for São Paulo’s municipal attorneys. Before approving them, the council should demand transparency about their cost and their justification in light of other public needs. An effective state needs well-paid professionals, but also clear priorities and respect for everyone’s money.
